summary: Los Angeles County steel lookout on Sawmill Mountain, built 1928-29, dismantled in 1934 and reportedly moved to Tejon Mountain; only cement blocks remain on the summit.

facts.design: 30-foot galvanized steel tower with a cabin for the lookout man
facts.status_note: Dismantled by November 1934; a hiking site says only cement blocks remain on the summit

access.note: Summit is on Angeles National Forest land; a hiking site gives a forest road route (FR 7N23) to it

events.note: Under construction per The Signal, March 1929. A November 1934 report says erected in 1928; a hiking site says established 1929.
Dismantled; the report says it did not fit the new detection plan

Forest Lookouts and a hiking site say the lookout was moved to Tejon Mountain in 1935. A county annual report says a Tejon Lookout Tower was erected in December 1936; unconfirmed that it is the same tower.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflicts: 1928 (1934 report) vs under construction March 1929 (The Signal); the event uses 1929. Elevation conflicts: The Signal gives 5,390 ft, Angeles Adventures 5517 ft; elevation not used in the story. Angeles Adventures calls it a Forest Service lookout; the story uses the county department named in the 1929 report. Tejon relocation is disputed: the county's 1936-37 report describes a Tejon tower erected in December 1936, and a Tejon site record dates piers to 1936; the story says it is unclear whether the Sawmill tower went there. Access rated public from a hiking site, not checked on the ground. Brief height 9.1 m and status gone are consistent with sources; no corrections proposed.
